result.response:
I have resolved the issue by ensuring the query's initial alias (base table) is initialized in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-301jihdl/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) in [compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-301jihdl/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py).

### Cause
When executing `Model.objects.all().delete()`, no filters have initialized `self.query.alias_map`, so `sum(self.query.alias_refcount[t] > 0 for t in self.query.alias_map)` evaluated to `0` (`!= 1`), causing `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias` to return `False` and fall back to generating a `DELETE ... WHERE pk IN (SELECT ...)` subquery.

### Solution
Call [`self.query.get_initial_alias()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-301jihdl/django/db/models/sql/query.py#L916-L926) in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-301jihdl/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) before counting active table aliases so that queries only targeting the base table use a direct `DELETE FROM` statement without a subquery.
